A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FigAgent, and all supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. However, v1 ends with references on page 10 and v2 on page 13; neither contains the repeatedly referenced appendix or supplementary material. Comparison of those promised implementation details and additional studies is therefore unavailable.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original figure-generation comparisons, qualitative examples, and component and evolution-operation ablations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original results on FigAgentBench and PaperBananaBench, component ablations, and a temporal middleware-update experiment in Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming tools as middlewares, v2 specifies concept merging and redundancy removal, adds regeneration using evaluator feedback when all candidate scores fall below a threshold, and changes the evolution objective to combine figure-level quality with individual middleware efficacy. V1's explicit ELK Planner stage is also absent from v2's presented pipeline, although its implementation status cannot be established from the missing supplementary material.

E1.justification: V2 adds reported evaluation on PaperBananaBench alongside its collected corpus, now called FigAgentBench. Both versions retain AI-paper method-illustration generation as the task. The additional benchmark expands dataset coverage, but the supplied material does not establish a distinct new task or substantially broader domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Nano, TikZero, and Paper2SysArch, removes DALLE and Paper2Any, and adds PaperBanana, AutoFigure, direct GPT-5 code generation, StarVector, and three pipelines combining image generators with EditBanana. This substantially changes the evaluated comparison set.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the agent backbone from GPT-4o to GPT-5 and the retrieval encoder from all-MiniLM-L6-v2 to all-mpnet-base-v2. The collected corpus changes from 4,692 to 4,964 pairs, retaining the 80/20 split. DiagramEval is now described as comparing generated figures with paper text rather than author-created figures, and VLM scoring is added. The temporal study introduces repository cutoffs and update controls while retaining the full test set.

E4.justification: V2 retains the original component and evolution-operation ablations, consolidating v1's Tables 3–4 into Table 3. It adds a greedy-selection control and a temporal study comparing a 2023 repository, direct additions, evolutionary updates, and rebuilding through 2025. Figure 2 also introduces marked structural and visual defects. Human evaluation and other supplementary analyses are mentioned but unavailable for verification.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both present point estimates; statements that components contribute significantly are not accompanied by statistical testing.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. Table 1 reports FigAgent NA/PA F1 of 54.2/46.2 in v1, versus 51.4/32.6 on FigAgentBench and 51.6/36.7 on PaperBananaBench in v2, with new VLM scores of 61.4 and 68.9. These are results under changed settings, not controlled performance declines. Baseline and ablation scores also change, and temporal-update results and new qualitative examples are added.

T1.justification: Equation 2 changes from a sum of individual tool-efficacy scores to the sum of mean generated-figure quality over a sampled batch and mean efficacy over invoked middlewares. This substantively revises the mathematical objective and its aggregation. The principal search criterion remains equivalent, and neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 explicitly claims novelty in identifying three characteristics of illustration generation. V2 drops that contribution and centers its novelty claim on a framework for middleware creation, evolution, and orchestration. The central claims of automatic high-fidelity SVG generation and state-of-the-art benchmark performance remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations about rarely invoked low-quality middlewares contaminating evolution and about evolutionary updates avoiding repository rebuilding and model-parameter changes. It also expands baseline-specific interpretations. However, its statement that AutoFigure improves over Nano is overgeneralized: on FigAgentBench, AutoFigure has better PA but worse NA F1 and VLM scores. Neither version supplies a dedicated limitations discussion.

D1.justification: V2 adds explicit middleware-parameter examples, XML extraction information, and a December 2025 collection cutoff. Conversely, v1's project hyperlink disappears, and its explicit beta=1 setting is no longer documented as an experimental setting; v2 gives that value only for Figure 1's toy example. Prompts and further implementation details remain deferred to unavailable supplementary material.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from a single-model versus multi-agent organization to image-generation versus SVG-code approaches. V2 adds substantive discussion of PaperBanana, AutoFigure, EditBanana, and additional vector-generation and evolutionary-agent work, while dropping the Paper2Poster and PresentAgent discussion. It also revises its characterization of Paper2SysArch and repositions novelty around direct high-fidelity SVG generation through middlewares.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are substantially rewritten. The title changes, MIF becomes MI, tool terminology becomes middleware terminology, and agents receive new abbreviations. Method exposition now presents creation and evolution before orchestration and search, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. Figure 1 is redrawn around the revised agent presentation, and Figure 2 replaces the circuit-timing example with a FitVid comparison, defect annotations, and additional examples. Table 1 expands to two benchmarks and VLM columns; evolution ablations are merged and a new temporal-study table is introduced. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for the existing claims through more relevant baselines, a second benchmark, a greedy-search control, and a temporal-update study. These address weaknesses in v1's evaluation of search and adaptation. The net gain is limited by losses in access and implementation information, an overgeneralized AutoFigure-versus-Nano interpretation, and unavailable supplementary evidence. The changed protocols do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.
